newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on late short covering rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on late short covering rally.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Friday in an active session, with a steady stream of late, technical buying and pre-weekend short covering lifting the complex from early lows.
February gained three cents to close at $2.824 per million British thermal units. March settled 2.4 cents higher at $2.557. Other deferreds ended up by 0.8 to 2.5 cents.

"We could move up (as shorts cover) ahead of the Feb expiry (Monday), and if it gets cold next week, physical and paper prices could rebound," said one Midwest trader, noting some forecasters were calling for cooler weather later next week.
Most expected a technical bounce after the 22 percent slide in the six previous sessions, but few expected the upside to be sustained without some protracted cold.

Technically, traders still still pegged key support in February at the Dec 31 low of $2.613. Psychological resistance was seen at $3.00, with better selling likely at $3.33, $3.64 and then $3.80-3.84.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend cash prices cratered Friday by more than 30 cents to about the $2.60 level. Midcontinent pipes slid a similar amount to the $2.50 area. Cold weather moving into the East boosted New York city gate weekend prices slightly to the $3.30s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose two cents to $2.274. NYMEX said an estimated 55,823 Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 52,885.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas expires on Monday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, February closed one cent higher at $2.61, while deferreds finished up by one-half to 1.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by two cents to 21.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 292 contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 361.
